Yes—very likely.

At 44.5° altitude, the Moon is comfortably high in the southwest (azimuth about 232°), so there is no horizon obstruction issue. A 28%-illuminated Moon is a fairly conspicuous crescent, and its separation from the Sun of about 64° means it is well away from the brightest part of the twilight sky.

Civil twilight can make a thin crescent harder than at night, but 28% illumination is not especially thin, and clear skies plus knowing where to look strongly favor visibility. With normal unaided vision, you should be able to spot it—though it may look pale or washed out compared with a nighttime Moon.

Look southwest, roughly halfway from the horizon to overhead (a little under 45° up).
